zh.title: 世界最大空軍飛行員數排名：美國37,000人居首，俄羅斯、中國分居二、三
zh.summary: Simple Flying引用World Population Review的統計，依機隊規模列出世界飛行員人數最多的五支空軍，美國以14,486架軍機與37,000名飛行員居首，俄羅斯與中國分居第二、第三，印度與日本隨後；文章並指出各國普遍面臨招募與人力缺口，飛行員人數隨機隊增減而波動。
body: 依Simple Flying引用的統計，前五名分別為美國14,486架軍機、37,000名飛行員；俄羅斯4,211架、4,000至5,000名；中國3,304架、約4,000名；印度2,296架、3,834名；日本1,459架、約2,000名。文章指出，各國飛行員人數大致略高於機隊規模，且會隨機隊增減而波動。
美國的37,000名飛行員中，空軍約13,000名，海軍與陸戰隊約10,000名飛行軍官與飛行員，陸軍航空約14,000名直升機飛行員，文章指出即使如此仍不足以滿足編制需求，戰機社群壓力尤其明顯。俄羅斯則自2022年烏克蘭戰事以來，因戰損、疲勞與資深軍官折損而出現人力缺口，訓練課程雖已縮短、教官也被推回第一線，補充速度仍落後於損耗。
中國人民解放軍空軍約有4,000名現役飛行員且持續擴張，遼寧艦與山東艦合計約有300名具備航艦起降資格的飛行員，新服役的福建艦完成測試後還需要至少200名。印度空軍編制4,239個座艙名額，但僅能填補約3,834個；日本航空自衛隊約2,000人具備飛行資格，僅占近50,000名制服與文職人員的一小部分，戰機飛行員飛F-15J或F-2，愈來愈多人直接轉換至F-35A。

en.title: World's largest air forces by pilot numbers: US leads with 37,000 pilots
en.summary: Citing World Population Review, Simple Flying ranks the world's air forces by pilot numbers, with the United States first at 37,000 pilots and 14,486 airframes, followed by Russia and China, then India and Japan; the article notes recruitment shortages and shifting fleet sizes behind the numbers.
body: The ranking puts the United States first with 14,486 airframes and 37,000 pilots, followed by Russia with 4,211 airframes and 4,000 to 5,000 pilots, China with 3,304 airframes and about 4,000 pilots, India with 2,296 airframes and 3,834 pilots, and Japan with 1,459 airframes and about 2,000 pilots. The article notes that staffing generally runs slightly above aircraft numbers and fluctuates as fleets shrink and grow.

Of the American total, about 13,000 pilots serve in the Air Force, about 10,000 flying officers and aviators serve across Navy and Marine Corps squadrons, and about 14,000 helicopter pilots serve in Army Aviation, yet the article reports that crewing requirements are still not met, with the fighter community under particular pressure. Russia, by contrast, has struggled since combat operations in Ukraine began in 2022, with aircraft losses, fatigue and the deaths of experienced officers creating roster gaps, even as training courses have been shortened and instructors pushed back to front-line units.

China's People's Liberation Army Air Force has about 4,000 active-duty pilots and keeps expanding, with the carriers Liaoning and Shandong together carrying around 300 deck-qualified pilots and the new Fujian needing at least 200 more once trials finish. India's Air Force is authorized for 4,239 cockpit billets but can fill only about 3,834, while Japan's Air Self-Defense Force has about 2,000 qualified flyers out of a uniformed and civilian workforce of nearly 50,000, with fighter pilots flying the F-15J or F-2 and a growing share moving straight to the F-35A.
